qToday.text: The morning login is the only recurring manual step, so the session card leads. Open question — should the deck auto-refresh, or stay a snapshot you reload deliberately?

q0.text: Overrides live here: quantity stepper, run/skip for the day, and per-tick exclusion. Every one writes an audit event. Should an override be allowed after the first fill, or frozen once the ladder has traded?

q1.text: One order per tick, one share each, nothing ever modified — a day is a list of small orders, not one repriced order. That contradicts PRD M21, which says preserve one order id across modifies. One of the two has to go.

q1b.text: With a 1-share slice and a 7-share day, all 7 orders are placed by tick 6 and the remaining 57 ticks do nothing. Should a tick reprice the orders already resting, or is placing-and-waiting the whole behaviour?

qDay.text: Any past day reconstructed from stored data alone — ranking, orders, depth snapshots, cash and audit under one trace id. This is the screen that proves the system is auditable years later.

q2.text: The holdings table is sorted by gap, so row 1 is tomorrow's buy. Should the unaffordable rows (LT here) carry an explicit 'priced out' state, or is the ranking enough?

q3.text: At ₹500/month the data subscription takes about 24% of the gain so far and under 1% of contributions. Small now — but the chart still plots value against contributions-plus-subscription, so the cost can never hide inside the return.

qReb.text: Validation rejects a whole row rather than selling part of it. Open question — should a row asking for more than you hold be rejected outright, or clamped to the available quantity with a warning?

q4.text: LT has not been bought in 76 days — its price exceeds a day's cash, so it stays first in the ranking and never gets reached. Does the model need a per-name 'accumulate over N days' rule, or is that what carry is for?

qCfg.text: Slice size is config, which is why the whole order model changes from one line here. A static IP mapped to the API key is the one gate before the first live order — the screen says so rather than hiding it in a runbook.

qLedger.text: Two ledgers on one screen: cash in and out, and shares in and out. The share side exists because a trade made directly in Kite is invisible to the engine — an unrecorded external buy has no cost basis, which silently corrupts FIFO and every realised gain after it.

qSignIn.text: Two factors, no bypass, no reset link — the only account here controls a brokerage. Click through the card: Continue goes to the code step, Verify fails once, then locks. The left panel says the thing that is easy to forget — the timers trade whether or not anyone is signed in, so a lockout is an inconvenience, not an outage.

qEnrol.text: First run, and the one screen whose secret can never be shown again. The recovery codes are hashed, so losing both them and the phone means a shell on the box through SSM. Open question — should enrolment force the static IP step before it lets you finish, or is a warning enough?

qKite.text: The four-stage strip exists to make one boundary obvious: the Zerodha password and TOTP are typed on Zerodha's page, never on ours, and request_token is worthless without the API secret. Press Re-connect to see the same screen with no session — four of the six capabilities go red. Static IP is still unregistered, which is why the mode badge reads PAPER.

qAwait.text: The failure path that actually costs money. A day that resumes at 11:35 starts at tick 22, not tick 0 — it inherits the ladder position the clock implies, because tick numbering follows the clock and not the session. Miss 15:00 and the day is SKIPPED with the full ₹2,600 carried. Open question — should the hourly reminders escalate as the cutoff nears?

mSign.text: The authenticator lives on this same phone, so you leave the app mid-form to fetch the code. The form has to survive that, which is a mobile-only problem the desktop screen never has.

mToday.text: The whole phone app in one screen: is it waiting for me, is it running, is anything wrong. Tap the primary button to walk the day forward — waiting → running. The stop is at the bottom, reachable but never the first thing your thumb finds.

mTrade.text: The screen the approval gate exists for. Quantity stepper, the ranking that justified the pick, and how stale the sheet is — because authorising at 14:00 a sheet built at 09:45 is the case worth designing for. Regenerate clears overrides: approving a sheet is approving that sheet.

mKite.text: Same boundary the desktop screen draws, told in three lines instead of four cards. The badge stays PAPER until the static IP is registered, so the phone never implies a power the system does not have yet.

mStop.text: Two lists, and the second matters more: what it does not do. Panic is when people assume a stop button sells. Press-and-hold rather than tap, because the cost of an accidental press is a day.
